issues.should_be: The written repair quote Q-2610-5283 (Garage Central Auto, issued 28/10/2026, customer Thomas Petit, VW Golf 2020, policy VER-1004) shows Total excl. VAT 1 366,67 €, VAT 20 % 273,33 €, TOTAL INCL. VAT 1 640,00 €. Contract Article 1 defines repair cost as the total including VAT on the quote. The 'around €900' figure in the email was only the garage's phone estimate, superseded by the attached written quote.
issues.evidence: repair_quote.pdf, 'TOTAL INCL. VAT 1 640,00 €' line; contract 2630#10414 page 1, Article 1 ('Repair cost: the total amount including VAT shown on the repair quote'); customer email ('around €900' phone estimate, 'the written quote is attached').

checks.sources_say: Customer email subject and signature give policy number VER-1004; the repair quote header also states 'Insurer: Veridia Insurance, policy VER-1004'; Policy Schedule policy_id is VER-1004.
checks.evidence: Customer email ('Policy number: VER-1004'); repair_quote.pdf header ('Insurer: Veridia Insurance, policy VER-1004'); Policy Schedule in claims system.

checks.sources_say: Policy Schedule lists coverages C1 (third-party liability) and C2 (collision damage). The email describes the policyholder hitting a post alone — damage to the insured vehicle after a collision — which is C2 per contract Article 2.
checks.evidence: Policy Schedule coverages array (C1, C2); customer email ('I hit a post... Nobody else was involved'); contract 2630#10414 page 2, Article 2 coverage table.

checks.sources_say: Email states the accident happened on 27 October 2026.
checks.evidence: Customer email: 'I hit a post in an underground car park on 27 October 2026.'

checks.sources_say: The claim email was received on 2026-10-28, one day after the incident — within the 5-day reporting deadline of contract Article 4.1.
checks.evidence: Email header 'Customer email received on 2026-10-28'; contract 2630#10414 page 2, Article 4.1.

checks.sources_say: The written repair quote Q-2610-5283 (Garage Central Auto, issued 28/10/2026, customer Thomas Petit, VW Golf 2020, policy VER-1004) shows Total excl. VAT 1 366,67 €, VAT 20 % 273,33 €, TOTAL INCL. VAT 1 640,00 €. Contract Article 1 defines repair cost as the total including VAT on the quote. The 'around €900' figure in the email was only the garage's phone estimate, superseded by the attached written quote.
checks.evidence: repair_quote.pdf, 'TOTAL INCL. VAT 1 640,00 €' line; contract 2630#10414 page 1, Article 1 ('Repair cost: the total amount including VAT shown on the repair quote'); customer email ('around €900' phone estimate, 'the written quote is attached').

checks.sources_say: The policyholder himself hit a fixed post in a car park with nobody else involved, so the authorised driver is at fault. This also means the Article 5.2 not-at-fault waiver does not apply and the standard €300 C2 deductible stands.
checks.evidence: Customer email ('I hit a post... Nobody else was involved'); contract 2630#10414 page 2, Article 5.2 and Article 2 C2 deductible €300.

checks.sources_say: The email explicitly says 'Nobody else was involved'; the damage is to a fixed post, not to another vehicle or person.

Consistent with no third party being involved; there is no third party to identify. The playbook rule on commercial-vehicle third parties is not triggered because no third party of any kind is involved.
checks.evidence: Customer email ('Nobody else was involved'); handler playbook (referral rule applies only when the other driver is a commercial vehicle — not applicable here).

checks.sources_say: The email attaches repair_quote.pdf and damage_photos.zip; damage_photos.zip is stored by the mailroom and counts as received. The quote belongs to this policyholder and vehicle (Thomas Petit, Volkswagen Golf 2020, registration FD-371-WS, policy VER-1004). For C2, contract Article 4.3 requires photos of the damage and a repair quote — both present; the signed accident report is required only when a third party is involved, which is not the case.
checks.evidence: Customer email attachment list; repair_quote.pdf customer/vehicle block; contract 2630#10414 page 2, Article 4.3 required-documents table for C2.

checks.sources_say: Nothing in the email or the quote indicates any Article 3 exclusion: no alcohol/drugs, the policyholder has held a licence since 2008-11-01 (valid), no racing, no intentional damage (single-vehicle collision with a post), and the damage is collision damage, not wear or mechanical failure.
checks.evidence: Customer email and repair_quote.pdf contain no exclusion indicators; contract 2630#10414 page 2, Article 3 exclusion list; Policy Schedule licence_date 2008-11-01.

verdict.summary: Approve the claim in principle (in time, C2 covered, documents complete, no exclusion, no playbook referral), but the recorded repair cost of €900 is wrong — the quote's total incl. VAT is €1,640.00 — so the payout must be recalculated and an independent assessor is required under Article 6.1 because the repair cost exceeds €1,500.
